source.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: Stopping at a dyadic grid point selects the increments ending there or earlier. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source.original_text:
Fix a positive time horizon T, a coarse level m and a fine level n at least m. Choose a coarse grid point τ. For any two real paths X and Y on nonnegative time, the fine-grid sum of products of their stopped increments equals the fine-grid prefix sum of their original increment products through τ.

The horizon T is positive. Both grids are regular dyadic partitions of [0,T].
The fine level n is at least the coarse level m. The cutoff may be any coarse grid point, including 0 and T.
The two paths are arbitrary real-valued functions of nonnegative time.

\sum_{i=0}^{2^n-1}\bigl(X_{\min(\tau,t_{i+1})}-X_{\min(\tau,t_i)}\bigr)\bigl(Y_{\min(\tau,t_{i+1})}-Y_{\min(\tau,t_i)}\bigr)=\sum_{i:\ t_{i+1}\le \tau}(X_{t_{i+1}}-X_{t_i})(Y_{t_{i+1}}-Y_{t_i}).

theorem anonymous_target
  {T : NNReal} (hT : 0 < T) {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n) (k : Fin (2 ^ m + 1)) (X Y : NNReal → ℝ) :
  have τ :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.SampledElementaryApproximation.regularGridTimes
      (AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.SampledElementaryApproximation.dyadicMesh T m) (2 ^ m) k;
  have t :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.SampledElementaryApproximation.regularGridTimes
      (AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.SampledElementaryApproximation.dyadicMesh T n) (2 ^ n);
  ∑ i,
      (X (Min.min τ (t i.succ)) - X (Min.min τ (t i.castSucc))) *
        (Y (Min.min τ (t i.succ)) - Y (Min.min τ (t i.castSucc))) =
    ∑ i, if t i.succ ≤ τ then (X (t i.succ) - X (t i.castSucc)) * (Y (t i.succ) - Y (t i.castSucc)) else 0

blind_reconstruction.text:
Horizon T; dyadic levels m,n; coarse-grid endpoint tau; arbitrary scalar functions X,Y; fine-grid increments stopped at tau.

T∈[0,infinity), T>0; m,n∈N with m≤n; k∈{0,...,2^m}; X,Y:[0,infinity)→R.

Assumptions: Only T>0 and m≤n. X and Y require no regularity, measurability, or stochastic assumptions.

Conclusion: Let tau=kT/2^m and t_i=iT/2^n for i=0,...,2^n. Then ∑_{i=0}^{2^n-1}(X(min(tau,t_{i+1}))-X(min(tau,t_i)))(Y(min(tau,t_{i+1}))-Y(min(tau,t_i))) = ∑_{i=0}^{2^n-1}1_{t_{i+1}≤tau}(X(t_{i+1})-X(t_i))(Y(t_{i+1})-Y(t_i)).

Quantifier order: For every T>0, m≤n, coarse node index k and pair X,Y, the displayed finite-sum identity holds.

Scope: Deterministic exact equality for a coarse-grid stopping value, including tau=0 and tau=T. The cutoff includes intervals whose right endpoint equals tau.

Constant dependencies: No existential constants.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.DyadicElementaryRefinement

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.DyadicCutoffIncrements

open scoped BigOperators NNReal
open ElementaryItoIntegral SampledElementaryApproximation DyadicElementaryRefinement

/-- Stopping both paths at a coarse grid point retains exactly the fine
cells whose right endpoints lie at or before that grid point. -/
theorem dyadic_sum_mul_stopped_increments_eq_prefix
    {T : ℝ≥0} (hT : 0 < T) {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n)
    (k : Fin (2 ^ m + 1)) (X Y : ℝ≥0 → ℝ) :
    let τ := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T m) (2 ^ m) k
    let t := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T n) (2 ^ n)
    (∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n),
      (X (min τ (t i.succ)) - X (min τ (t i.castSucc))) *
        (Y (min τ (t i.succ)) - Y (min τ (t i.castSucc)))) =
    ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n), if t i.succ ≤ τ then
      (X (t i.succ) - X (t i.castSucc)) * (Y (t i.succ) - Y (t i.castSucc)) else 0 := by
  intro τ t
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i _
  let j := coarseCell hmn i
  have hstep : t i.castSucc < t i.succ :=
    regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT n) _ (Fin.castSucc_lt_succ)
  by_cases h : j.val < k.val
  · have hj : j.succ ≤ k := Nat.succ_le_iff.2 h
    have hright : t i.succ ≤ τ :=
      (fine_right_endpoint_le_coarse_right (T := T) hmn i).trans
        ((regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT m) _).monotone hj)
    rw [if_pos hright, min_eq_right hright, min_eq_right (hstep.le.trans hright)]
  · have hj : k ≤ j.castSucc := Nat.le_of_not_gt h
    have hleft : τ ≤ t i.castSucc :=
      ((regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT m) _).monotone hj).trans
        (coarse_left_endpoint_le_fine_left (T := T) hmn i)
    rw [if_neg (not_le.mpr (hleft.trans_lt hstep)), min_eq_left (hleft.trans hstep.le), min_eq_left hleft]
    simp

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.DyadicCutoffIncrements

lesson.statement: Fix a positive time horizon T, a coarse level m and a fine level n at least m. Choose a coarse grid point τ. For any two real paths X and Y on nonnegative time, the fine-grid sum of products of their stopped increments equals the fine-grid prefix sum of their original increment products through τ.
assumptions: The horizon T is positive. Both grids are regular dyadic partitions of [0,T].
The fine level n is at least the coarse level m. The cutoff may be any coarse grid point, including 0 and T.
The two paths are arbitrary real-valued functions of nonnegative time.

steps.title: Find the coarse cell containing each fine cell
steps.text: A fine cell is contained in the coarse cell with index j given by dyadic refinement. If the cutoff is the kth coarse grid point, that cell lies on one side of the cutoff.
steps.lean:
intro τ t
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i _
  let j := coarseCell hmn i
  have hstep : t i.castSucc < t i.succ :=
    regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT n) _ (Fin.castSucc_lt_succ)

steps.title: Evaluate the stopped increment on either side
steps.text: If j is smaller than k, both endpoints keep their original time. Otherwise both endpoints are mapped to τ, and the increment is zero. The inequality on the right endpoint includes a fine cell that ends exactly at τ.
steps.lean:
by_cases h : j.val < k.val
  · have hj : j.succ ≤ k := Nat.succ_le_iff.2 h
    have hright : t i.succ ≤ τ :=
      (fine_right_endpoint_le_coarse_right (T := T) hmn i).trans
        ((regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT m) _).monotone hj)
    rw [if_pos hright, min_eq_right hright, min_eq_right (hstep.le.trans hright)]
  · have hj : k ≤ j.castSucc := Nat.le_of_not_gt h
    have hleft : τ ≤ t i.castSucc :=
      ((regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT m) _).monotone hj).trans
        (coarse_left_endpoint_le_fine_left (T := T) hmn i)
    rw [if_neg (not_le.mpr (hleft.trans_lt hstep)), min_eq_left (hleft.trans hstep.le), min_eq_left hleft]
    simp

lesson.lean_statement: The right-hand side uses a sum over all fine cell indices with an if on the right endpoint. The two endpoint indices are i.castSucc and i.succ.
lesson.lean_proof: Dyadic refinement gives the enclosing coarse cell. Its order relative to the cutoff resolves both the condition and the stopped times, pointwise.
